name: Altadena
science: Curiosity's 43rd drill hole, in the boxwork bedrock: its powder went to the CheMin and SAM labs.
risk: Gentle bedrock, slopes under 8° around it: the closest stop, 200 m from the habitat.
tagSource: NASA Curiosity blog, sols 4568-4569: drill hole image of 8 Jun 2025 (sol 4564)
scienceSource: NASA Curiosity blog, sols 4568-4569 (planning date 11 Jun 2025): Altadena drill hole imaged on sol 4564 (8 Jun 2025), sample delivered to CheMin and SAM, '42 drill sites that came before'
taskSource: Task times proposed from NASA/TP-2017-219457, table 30 (same set as Valle de la Luna)

name: Valle de la Luna
science: Curiosity's 44th drill hole, in the Monte Grande hollow: is the hollow rock different from the ridges?
risk: Floor of a hollow, 2 m below the ridge next to it; edges up to 18° slope.
tagSource: Drill sols from the NASA Curiosity blog; Earth dates from the REMS feed (sol 4693 = 2025-10-19, sol 4718 = 2025-11-13)
scienceSource: NASA Curiosity blog, sols 4695-4701 (13 Nov 2025): drill hole 44 inside the Monte Grande hollow
taskSource: Task times proposed from NASA/TP-2017-219457, table 30

name: Nevado Sajama
science: Drilled on a boxwork ridge top, 10 m from Valle de la Luna: ridge rock versus hollow rock.
risk: Ridge top, 2 m above the hollow; slopes up to 18° on the way up.
tagSource: Drill sols from the NASA Curiosity blog; Earth dates from the REMS feed (sol 4693 = 2025-10-19, sol 4718 = 2025-11-13)
scienceSource: NASA Curiosity blog, sols 4716-4722 (18 Nov 2025): drilled on top of a ridge, Navcam sol 4718
taskSource: Task times proposed from NASA/TP-2017-219457, table 30
nameOrigin: NASA named the target after an extinct volcano, the highest peak in Bolivia

name: Campo Marte
science: Drill hole in the layered sulfate unit just above the boxwork; ChemCam and APXS measured it first.
risk: Loose blocks: next door at Atacama the drilled rock came up with the drill. 77 m above the habitat.
tagSource: NASA Curiosity blog, sols 4900-4907: drill hole image of 16 May 2026 (sol 4897)
scienceSource: NASA Curiosity blog, sols 4893-4899 (planning date 15 May 2026): same stratum as Atacama, 'the layered sulfate unit above the boxwork structures'; sols 4900-4907: first colour look of the drill hole, 16 May 2026 (sol 4897)
taskSource: Task times proposed from NASA/TP-2017-219457, table 30 (same set as Valle de la Luna)
nameOrigin: NASA named it after a natural red sandstone feature in Bolivia: 'Field of Mars'
